Murine CRC models with intestinal-specific Kras G12D/+ knockin Eight-week-old mice were used to establish transgenic intestinal-specific Kras knockin mice (Kras G12D/+ Villin-Cre, Kras G12D/+ Cdx2-Cre ERT2 ). For Kras G12D/+ Cdx2-Cre ERT2 mice, tamoxifen (100 mg/kg) was intraperitoneally injected into the mice to activate the expression of oncogenic Kras G12D/+ . Wildtype littermates (Kras G12D/+ ) were used as controls. For tumorigenesis model, 8-weekold intestine-specific Kras G12D (Kras G12D/+ Villin-Cre) mice and wildtype littermates (Kras G12D/+ ) were given a single intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection of 10 mg/kg azoxymethane (AOM). After 7 days, mice were treated with three cycles of 2% DSS in drinking water, with a 5-day dextran sodium sulfate (DSS) regimen followed by a 16-day break. We generated intestine-specific Kras G12D mice by crossing LSL-Kras G12D mice to Villin-Cre mice, with wildtype littermates as controls. Stool samples were collected at 2, 6, and 12 months. Finally, these mice were sacrificed, and their colon mucosa samples were collected at 12 months. Furthermore, we generated conditioned Kras G12D/+ CDX-CreERT2 mice. We collected stool samples at 2, 4, and 8 weeks and colon at 8 weeks. All samples were snap-frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored at -80 • C.
